To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have prepared two new complexes of platinum with Pt-C bonds, one of which has a novel rearranged ring system.

the reaction of the dication [Pt(2) (μ-S)(2) (PPh(3)) (4)] with 1,3-diacylpropanes leads to the formation of novel dicationic complexes containing Pt-C bonds, and that the rearrangement of one of the complexes is accompanied by a change in ring size from 6.6.6 to 6.5.4.

the reaction of [Pt(3)(μ-S)(3)(PPh(2))(4)] with 2,4-DNP derivatives of 1,1- or 1,3- dichloroacetone results in the formation of a novel [6.5,5] bicyclical di-μ-thiodiacetone complex containing a Pt-C bond and a Pt(3)S(3) ring.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the synthesis and characterisation of novel Pt(II) complexes containing Pt-C bonds and the development of new synthetic routes to such species.
the development of a range of novel Pt(II) compounds containing thiolate ligands and with the study of the reactions of these complexes.
the development of new methods for the synthesis and structural characterisation of transition metal complexes, and with their use to prepare novel organometallic compounds.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
[Pt(2)μ-S(2)PPh(3)](4)] is a versatile precursor to complexes containing Pt-C bonds.

the reaction of [Pt(μ-S)(2)PPh(3)(4)] with 1,3-bis(chloromethylene)acetone derivatives leads to the formation of novel rearranged complexes in which a Pt-C bond is formed and the Pt(μ-S)(μ-C)Pt core is part of a [6.5.n] bicyclic ring system (n = 5, 6).
the Pt(2)S(2)P(4) core can be considered to be a highly reactive and dynamic structural motif.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Pt-S bond is a strong bond and the Pt-S-Pt angle is a strong bond angle.
the reaction of [Pt(μ-S)(PPh(2))](4) with ClCH(2)(CH(2)(C(O)Cl)CH(2)(S) gives the novel complex [Pt(μ-SC(3)H(4)C(O)S)(P(2)Ph(4))] in which there is a novel Pt-C bond.
the Pt-S-C-Pt five-membered ring system is unstable and readily rearranges to the Pt-S-Pt-C five-membered system.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Pt(II)-C bond is sufficiently robust for use in the synthesis of novel Pt(II) complexes, but not sufficiently stable for use in catalysis.

the [Pt(2)S(2)(PPh3)(4)](2) core can undergo a variety of structural rearrangements, some of which have not been observed in other platinum complexes.
